$comment: Read from the SIA chart set AD 2 LFJD (AIP France, chart dated 2025-09-04): the reporting points come from the coordinates table of the chart,
the notes from the English column of its text pages, both read by a script and checked (each point lies within 80 NM of the aerodrome).
Only what the chart prints is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text. Drawings (circuit, routes, radials) are not read.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.

A "fr" object holds the French column of the same chart for the notes, copied as printed and never translated: a French note sits at the index of its English twin and is left empty when the twin could not be paired with certainty.

The reporting points are in French: "location" is the name printed in the French column of the chart, copied and not translated, and "purpose" is written in French; a point whose French name could not be read has no "location". Only "spoken.en" is English: the name the English phraseology says over the radio.
name: Corlier

source.extraction: chart text, table and English column read by script, checked
source.frenchExtraction: French column of the chart text, read by script and paired with the English sentences

notes: AD reserved for radio-equipped ACFT.
Aircraft pilots must hold a valid mountain license or altiport access authorization.
AD usable without restriction for HEL.
ULM: it is strongly recommended to have attended the mountain course organized by the FFPLUM.
Commercial air transport is prohibited with the exception of discovery flights.
Caution advised with south wind (risk of turbulence).
Snow clearance not provided.
After heavy rains, check runway condition with the AD operator.
Arrive via point W at 3100 ft AMSL without interfering with the aerodrome circuit, then follow the circuit indicated on the chart to join overhead.
Fly the aerodrome traffic circuit at 3100 ft AMSL.
Do not park in line-up and take-off positions.
AD réservé aux ACFT munis de radio.
Les pilotes d'avions doivent être titulaires de la qualification montagne ou de l'autorisation d'accès à l'altiport en état de validité.
L'AD est utilisable sans restriction par les HEL.
ULM : il est fortement recommandé d'avoir suivi le cursus montagne organisé par la FFPLUM.
Le transport aérien commercial par avion est interdit à l'exception des vols de découverte.
Prudence recommandée par vent de Sud (risques de turbulences).
Déneigement non assuré.
Après de fortes pluies, s'assurer de l'état de la piste auprès de l'exploitant.
Arriver par W à 3100 ft AMSL sans interférer avec le circuit d'aérodrome puis suivre le tracé figuré sur la carte pour rejoindre la verticale.
Effectuer le circuit d'aérodrome à 3100 ft AMSL.
Ne pas stationner en position alignement de décollage.
